This is a reverse-engineering benchmark. You are given a compiled binary and its documentation.
Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that simply makes the provided binary executable (`chmod +x ./executable`) or copies it (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace

# flamelens

flamelens is an interactive flamegraph viewer for the terminal.

Description

flamelens reads folded stacks (stack traces aggregated in the "folded" format) and
renders an interactive flamegraph in a terminal UI so you can explore profiling data
without opening a browser.

Usage

Run flamelens with a folded stacks filename, or pipe folded stacks data to it:

flamelens <folded-stacks-filename>

or

cat folded-stacks.txt | flamelens

Live mode

flamelens can attach to a running process to display a live flamegraph (when supported):

flamelens --pid <pid-of-process>

Viewing perf data

You can generate folded stacks from perf and pipe them to flamelens, for example:

perf script -i perf.data | <tool-to-collapse-perf-output> | flamelens

Key bindings

- h/j/k/l or arrow keys: Navigate cursor for frame selection
- f: Scroll down
- b: Scroll up
- G: Scroll to bottom
- g: Scroll to top
- Enter: Zoom in on the selected frame
- Esc: Reset zoom
- /<regex>: Find and highlight frames matching the regex
- #: Find and highlight frames matching the selected frame
- n: Jump to next match
- N: Jump to previous match
- r: Reset to default view
- z (in Live mode): Freeze the flamegraph
- q (or Ctrl + c): Exit

Examples

- Open a folded stacks file:

  flamelens folded.txt

- Pipe collapsed perf output:

  perf script -i perf.data | inferno-collapse-perf | flamelens

Notes

This README intentionally omits build- and implementation-specific details.

# flamelens

flamelens is an interactive flamegraph viewer for the terminal.

Description

flamelens reads folded stacks (stack traces aggregated in the "folded" format) and
renders an interactive flamegraph in a terminal UI so you can explore profiling data
without opening a browser.

Usage

Run flamelens with a folded stacks filename, or pipe folded stacks data to it:

flamelens <folded-stacks-filename>

or

cat folded-stacks.txt | flamelens

Live mode

flamelens can attach to a running process to display a live flamegraph (when supported):

flamelens --pid <pid-of-process>

Viewing perf data

You can generate folded stacks from perf and pipe them to flamelens, for example:

perf script -i perf.data | <tool-to-collapse-perf-output> | flamelens

Key bindings

- h/j/k/l or arrow keys: Navigate cursor for frame selection
- f: Scroll down
- b: Scroll up
- G: Scroll to bottom
- g: Scroll to top
- Enter: Zoom in on the selected frame
- Esc: Reset zoom
- /<regex>: Find and highlight frames matching the regex
- #: Find and highlight frames matching the selected frame
- n: Jump to next match
- N: Jump to previous match
- r: Reset to default view
- z (in Live mode): Freeze the flamegraph
- q (or Ctrl + c): Exit

Examples

- Open a folded stacks file:

  flamelens folded.txt

- Pipe collapsed perf output:

  perf script -i perf.data | inferno-collapse-perf | flamelens

Notes

This README intentionally omits build- and implementation-specific details.

import pty, os, subprocess, select, time, sys

def run_pty(args, inp_data=None, timeout=6):
    # Use `script` or python pty to run with terminal
    # We'll spawn process with pty for stdin/stdout/stderr?
    # Easiest: use `unbuffer`? Let's do pty.spawn-like manual.
    master, slave = pty.openpty()
    # slave will be stdin/stdout/stderr
    import subprocess
    p = subprocess.Popen(["./executable"]+args, stdin=slave, stdout=slave, stderr=slave, text=False, close_fds=True)
    os.close(slave)
    # optionally send input? For file arg case no need
    # set nonblock and read
    import fcntl
    flags = fcntl.fcntl(master, fcntl.F_GETFL)
    fcntl.fcntl(master, fcntl.F_SETFL, flags | os.O_NONBLOCK)
    output = b""
    start = time.time()
    # if inp_data and args empty (stdin pipe), we need to feed via master? But master is terminal, feeding would be like typing.
    # For file-based test, just read.
    # We'll send inp_data after short delay if provided
    if inp_data:
        time.sleep(0.5)
        os.write(master, inp_data)
        #time.sleep(0.2)
    while time.time()-start < timeout:
        try:
            r,_,_ = select.select([master], [], 0.5)
            if r:
                try:
                    data = os.read(master, 4096)
                    if not data:
                        break
                    output += data
                except OSError as e:
                    #print("read err",e)
                    break
        except Exception as e:
            print("sel err",e)
            break
        # check if process exited?
        if p.poll() is not None:
            # drain remaining
            time.sleep(0.3)
            try:
                while True:
                    r,_,_ = select.select([master], [], 0.2)
                    if not r:
                        break
                    data = os.read(master, 4096)
                    if not data:
                        break
                    output+=data
            except: break
            break
    # try to kill
    try:
        p.terminate()
        time.sleep(0.2)
        p.kill()
    except: pass
    os.close(master)
    try:
        p.wait(timeout=1)
    except: pass
    return output, p.returncode

import tempfile
folded = b"main;foo;bar 10\nmain;foo;baz 20\n"
with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(mode='wb', delete=False, suffix='.txt') as f:
    f.write(folded)
    fname=f.name
print("fname",fname)
out, code = run_pty([fname], timeout=5)
print(f"FILE PTY code={code} out len {len(out)}")
print(out[:8000].decode(errors='replace'))
print("---END---")
PY

import pty, os, subprocess, select, time, fcntl, struct, termios, sys, tempfile, re

def run_capture(args, input_file_content=None, filename=None, keys=b"", rows=24, cols=80, timeout=4, wait_before_keys=0.8, extra_wait=0.8):
    # if filename is None and input_file_content is not None, create temp file
    # if input_file_content is bytes and filename == "STDIN", we need to pipe via file? Actually stdin vs file: for stdin test we need to run with stdin as pipe but stdout as tty? 
    # Our current harness uses same pty for stdin/out. For stdin data test, original reads from stdin non-blocking? How to provide stdin data via pty typing? 
    # Alternative: provide file.
    created=None
    if input_file_content is not None and filename is None:
        tf=tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(mode='wb', delete=False, suffix='.txt')
        tf.write(input_file_content)
        tf.close()
        filename=tf.name
        created=filename
        args = args + [filename] if filename not in args else args
    # if filename == "STDIN_PIPE", we need separate handling: stdin pipe, stdout pty
    # We'll handle separately in another function
    master, slave = pty.openpty()
    winsz = struct.pack("HHHH", rows, cols, 0, 0)
    fcntl.ioctl(slave, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, winsz)
    # need to pass args correctly
    p = subprocess.Popen(["./executable"]+args, stdin=slave, stdout=slave, stderr=slave, text=False, close_fds=True)
    os.close(slave)
    flags = fcntl.fcntl(master, fcntl.F_GETFL)
    fcntl.fcntl(master, fcntl.F_SETFL, flags | os.O_NONBLOCK)
    output=b""
    start=time.time()
    # wait a bit then send keys
    time.sleep(wait_before_keys)
    # drain initial
    while True:
        r,_,_ = select.select([master], [], [], 0.2)
        if not r:
            break
        try:
            d=os.read(master, 16384)
            if not d: break
            output+=d
        except: break
    if keys:
        #print(f"sending {keys!r}", file=sys.stderr)
        try:
            os.write(master, keys)
        except Exception as e:
            print("write err",e)
        time.sleep(extra_wait)
        while True:
            r,_,_ = select.select([master], [], [], 0.3)
            if not r:
                break
            try:
                d=os.read(master, 16384)
                if not d: break
                output+=d
            except: break
    else:
        # just wait a bit more to ensure stable
        time.sleep(0.3)
    try:
        # send q to exit cleanly? Actually we will terminate; but try to capture exit behavior
        pass
    except: pass
    try:
        p.terminate()
        time.sleep(0.3)
        if p.poll() is None:
            p.kill()
    except: pass
    # drain after termination? alternate screen restore may emit
    try:
        while True:
            r,_,_ = select.select([master], [], [], 0.2)
            if not r: break
            try:
                d=os.read(master, 16384)
                if not d: break
                output+=d
            except: break
    except: pass
    try: os.close(master)
    except: pass
    try: p.wait(timeout=1)
    except: pass
    if created:
        try: os.unlink(created)
        except: pass
    return output

def parse_screen(raw):
    # crude: extract positioned writes. Ratatui uses \x1b[{r};{c}H then text with SGR colors.
    # We'll strip SGR and reconstruct grid rows/cols 24x80
    # For now just strip escapes and show lines?
    # Better to use tmux style: we can decode final screen by applying cursor moves.
    # Simplified: split by \x1b[ ... H and \x1b[2J etc.
    # Let's just return raw decode with escapes made visible for analysis, plus stripped text.
    txt=raw.decode(errors='replace')
    # strip SGR: \x1b\[[0-9;]*m
    import re
    stripped=re.sub(r'\x1b\[[0-9;]*m', '', txt)
    # also remove \x1b\[.*?H cursor moves? Keep them as newline markers
    # Replace \x1b\[2J with <CLS>, \x1b\[\?1049h etc.
    stripped2=re.sub(r'\x1b\[\?[0-9]+[a-z]', '', stripped)
    stripped2=stripped2.replace('\x1b[?25l','').replace('\x1b[?25h','')
    # Now cursor positioning: \x1b\[(\d+);(\d+)H
    # We can reconstruct grid
    return txt, stripped2

if __name__=="__main__":
    # test simple
    out=run_capture([], input_file_content=b"main;foo;bar 10\nmain;foo;baz 20\n")
    txt, stripped = parse_screen(out)
    print("RAW len",len(out))
    print(txt[:5000])
    print("---STRIPPED---")
    print(repr(stripped[:5000]))
    print(stripped[:5000])

                if not d: break

import pty, os, subprocess, select, time, fcntl, struct, termios, tempfile, re

def run_with_keys(args, keys_list=None, rows=24, cols=80, init_wait=0.8, key_wait=0.6):
    """
    keys_list: list of bytes to send sequentially, each with key_wait delay
    Returns raw output bytes and exit code (if exited via q, else None and terminated)
    Captures all output for fixed durations, not until silence.
    """
    master, slave = pty.openpty()
    winsz = struct.pack("HHHH", rows, cols, 0, 0)
    fcntl.ioctl(slave, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, winsz)
    p = subprocess.Popen(["./executable"]+args, stdin=slave, stdout=slave, stderr=slave)
    os.close(slave)
    flags = fcntl.fcntl(master, fcntl.F_GETFL)
    fcntl.fcntl(master, fcntl.F_SETFL, flags | os.O_NONBLOCK)
    out=b""
    def drain(duration):
        nonlocal out
        end=time.time()+duration
        while time.time()<end:
            r,_,_ = select.select([master], [], [], max(0, end-time.time()))
            if not r:
                break
            try:
                d=os.read(master, 16384)
                if not d:
                    break
                out+=d
            except OSError:
                break
            # if process exited, keep draining a bit
            if p.poll() is not None:
                # drain remaining quickly
                time.sleep(0.2)
                while True:
                    r2,_,_ = select.select([master], [], [], 0.1)
                    if not r2: break
                    try:
                        d=os.read(master, 16384)
                        if not d: break
                        out+=d
                    except: break
                break
    drain(init_wait)
    exited=False
    if keys_list:
        for k in keys_list:
            if p.poll() is not None:
                break
            try:
                os.write(master, k)
            except Exception as e:
                print(f"write err {e}")
                break
            drain(key_wait)
    # check exit
    code=p.poll()
    # if not exited, terminate
    if code is None:
        try:
            p.terminate()
            time.sleep(0.3)
            if p.poll() is None:
                p.kill()
            # drain restore
            end=time.time()+0.5
            while time.time()<end:
                r,_,_ = select.select([master], [], [], 0.2)
                if not r: break
                try:
                    d=os.read(master, 16384)
                    if not d: break
                    out+=d
                except: break
        except: pass
    else:
        # already exited, drain already done
        pass
    try: os.close(master)
    except: pass
    try: p.wait(timeout=1)
    except: pass
    return out, p.returncode

def grid_from_raw(raw, rows=24, cols=80):
    txt = raw.decode(errors='replace')
    grid = [[' ']*cols for _ in range(rows)]
    cur_r, cur_c = 0,0
    i=0
    n=len(txt)
    while i<n:
        if txt[i]=='\x1b' and i+1<n and txt[i+1]=='[':
            j=i+2
            while j<n and (txt[j].isdigit() or txt[j] in ';?:'):
                j+=1
            if j>=n:
                break
            cmd=txt[j]
            params=txt[i+2:j]
            if cmd=='H':
                if ';' in params:
                    try:
                        r,c = params.split(';')
                        cur_r=int(r)-1
                        cur_c=int(c)-1
                    except: pass
                elif params=='':
                    cur_r,cur_c=0,0
            elif cmd=='J':
                if params=='2':
                    grid=[[' ']*cols for _ in range(rows)]
                    cur_r,cur_c=0,0
            elif cmd=='K':
                # clear line? ratatui may use? handle: clear from cursor to end?
                pass
            i=j+1
        elif txt[i]=='\x1b' and i+1<n and txt[i+1]=='(':
            i+=3
        elif txt[i]=='\x1b' and txt[i+1]=='M':
            # reverse line? ignore
            i+=2
        else:
            ch=txt[i]
            if ch=='\n':
                cur_r+=1;cur_c=0
            elif ch=='\r':
                cur_c=0
            else:
                # handle unicode? Our grid is char-based, but terminal is column-based with wide chars? For now, treat each unicode char as 1 col (but box drawing is 1 col)
                if 0<=cur_r<rows and 0<=cur_c<cols:
                    grid[cur_r][cur_c]=ch
                    cur_c+=1
                    if cur_c>=cols:
                        cur_c=0;cur_r+=1
            i+=1
            continue
        # for escape, already advanced
    return [''.join(row) for row in grid]

def show_grid(grid):
    for idx,line in enumerate(grid, start=1):
        # rstrip trailing spaces for display but keep box
        print(f"{idx:2d}|{line}|")

if __name__=="__main__":
    import tempfile
    content=b"main;foo;bar 10\nmain;foo;baz 20\nmain;qux 5\n"
    tf=tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(mode='wb', delete=False, suffix='.txt')
    tf.write(content); tf.close()
    fname=tf.name
    out, code = run_with_keys([fname], keys_list=[b"j"])
    print(f"code {code} len {len(out)}")
    grid=grid_from_raw(out)
    show_grid(grid)
    os.unlink(fname)

use std::io;

#[cfg(feature = "libc")]
use libc::size_t;
#[cfg(not(feature = "libc"))]
use rustix::fd::{AsFd, AsRawFd, BorrowedFd, OwnedFd, RawFd};
#[cfg(feature = "libc")]
use std::{
    fs,
    marker::PhantomData,
    os::unix::{
        io::{IntoRawFd, RawFd},
        prelude::AsRawFd,
    },
};

/// A file descriptor wrapper.
///
/// It allows to retrieve raw file descriptor, write to the file descriptor and
/// mainly it closes the file descriptor once dropped.
#[derive(Debug)]
#[cfg(feature = "libc")]
pub struct FileDesc<'a> {
    fd: RawFd,
    close_on_drop: bool,
    phantom: PhantomData<&'a ()>,
}

#[cfg(not(feature = "libc"))]
pub enum FileDesc<'a> {
    Owned(OwnedFd),
    Borrowed(BorrowedFd<'a>),
}

#[cfg(feature = "libc")]
impl FileDesc<'_> {
    /// Constructs a new `FileDesc` with the given `RawFd`.
    ///
    /// # Arguments
    ///
    /// * `fd` - raw file descriptor
    /// * `close_on_drop` - specify if the raw file descriptor should be closed once the `FileDesc` is dropped
    pub fn new(fd: RawFd, close_on_drop: bool) -> FileDesc<'static> {
        FileDesc {
            fd,
            close_on_drop,
            phantom: PhantomData,
        }
    }

    pub fn read(&self, buffer: &mut [u8]) -> io::Result<usize> {
        let result = unsafe {
            libc::read(
                self.fd,
                buffer.as_mut_ptr() as *mut libc::c_void,
                buffer.len() as size_t,
            )
        };

        if result < 0 {
            Err(io::Error::last_os_error())
        } else {

    txt=out.decode(errors='replace')
    # Find flame rows: rows 4,5,6,7 etc. They are after \x1b[4;1H, \x1b[5;1H etc.
    # Extract each row's raw segment
    # Pattern: \x1b\[(\d+);1H + SGR + text
    # For simplicity, split by cursor moves and look at rows 4-7
    rows={}
    # Find all occurrences of \x1b\[(\d+);1H(.*?)(?=\x1b\[|\Z) ??? Need to parse sequentially
    # Instead, use grid reconstruction + also parse widths via grid? Grid loses color boundaries, but we can infer widths by where names appear? Better to parse raw SGR segments.
    # Let's just print raw for manual analysis
    print(txt[:8000])
    print("---")
    # Also try to extract block widths by looking at SGR + spaces
    # Each block is: \x1b[38;2;...;48;2;R;G;Bm + text (name + padding)
    # Text length should equal block width
    pat = re.compile(r'\x1b\[38;2;.*?48;2;(.*?m)(.*?)(?=\x1b\[38|\x1b\[1m\x1b\[38;5)')
    # Actually simpler: find all flame blocks
    # Look for flame rows specifically: after \x1b\[4;1H etc.
    # Let's extract row by row
    # Find row markers
    markers = list(re.finditer(r'\x1b\[(\d+);1H', txt))
    for m in markers:
        row=int(m.group(1))
        if 4<=row<=8:
            start=m.end()
            # find next marker or end
            idx = txt.find('\x1b[', start)
            # Actually next marker is next \x1b\[...H or \x1b\[1m...

    print(f"\n=== CONTENT {content!r} ===")
    get_blocks(content)

import pty, os, subprocess, select, time, fcntl, struct, termios, tempfile
def run_bulk(args, bulk_keys=b"", rows=24, cols=80, init_wait=0.8, final_wait=0.8):
    master, slave = pty.openpty()
    winsz = struct.pack("HHHH", rows, cols, 0, 0)
    fcntl.ioctl(slave, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, winsz)
    p = subprocess.Popen(["./executable"]+args, stdin=slave, stdout=slave, stderr=slave)
    os.close(slave)
    flags = fcntl.fcntl(master, fcntl.F_GETFL)
    fcntl.fcntl(master, fcntl.F_SETFL, flags | os.O_NONBLOCK)
    out=b""
    def drain(dur):
        nonlocal out
        end=time.time()+dur
        while time.time()<end:
            r,_,_ = select.select([master], [], [], max(0, end-time.time()))
            if not r: break
            try:
                d=os.read(master, 16384)
                if not d: break
                out+=d
            except: break
            if p.poll() is not None:
                time.sleep(0.2)
                while True:
                    r2,_,_ = select.select([master], [], [], 0.1)
                    if not r2: break
                    try:
                        d=os.read(master, 16384)
                        if not d: break
                        out+=d
                    except: break
                break
    drain(init_wait)
    if bulk_keys:
        try: os.write(master, bulk_keys)
        except: pass
        drain(final_wait)
    code=p.poll()
    if code is None:
        try:
            p.terminate()
            time.sleep(0.3)
            if p.poll() is None: p.kill()
            end=time.time()+0.5
            while time.time()<end:
                r,_,_ = select.select([master], [], [], 0.2)
                if not r: break
                try:
                    d=os.read(master, 16384)
                    if not d: break
                    out+=d
                except: break
        except: pass
    try: os.close(master)
    except: pass
    try: p.wait(timeout=1)
    except: pass
    return out, p.returncode

def grid_from_raw(raw, rows=24, cols=80):
    txt = raw.decode(errors='replace')
    grid = [[' ']*cols for _ in range(rows)]
    cur_r, cur_c = 0,0
    i=0
    n=len(txt)
    while i<n:
        if txt[i]=='\x1b' and i+1<n and txt[i+1]=='[':
            j=i+2
            while j<n and (txt[j].isdigit() or txt[j] in ';?:'):
                j+=1
            if j>=n: break
            cmd=txt[j]
            params=txt[i+2:j]
            if cmd=='H':
                if ';' in params:
                    r,c = params.split(';')
                    cur_r=int(r)-1;cur_c=int(c)-1
                elif params=='': cur_r,cur_c=0,0
            elif cmd=='J':
                if params=='2':
                    grid=[[' ']*cols for _ in range(rows)];cur_r,cur_c=0,0
            i=j+1
        elif txt[i]=='\x1b' and i+1<n and txt[i+1]=='(':
            i+=3
        else:
            ch=txt[i]
            if ch=='\n': cur_r+=1;cur_c=0
            elif ch=='\r': cur_c=0
            else:
                if 0<=cur_r<rows and 0<=cur_c<cols:
                    grid[cur_r][cur_c]=ch;cur_c+=1
                    if cur_c>=cols: cur_c=0;cur_r+=1
            i+=1
    return [''.join(row) for row in grid]

import sys
sys.path.insert(0,'/tmp')
from harness2 import run_bulk, grid_from_raw
import tempfile, os, re
def cap_raw(content):
    tf=tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(mode='wb', delete=False, suffix='.txt')
    tf.write(content); tf.close()
    fname=tf.name
    out, code = run_bulk([fname], bulk_keys=b"")
    grid=grid_from_raw(out)
    print(f"content {content!r} -> sel:{grid[21].strip()}")
    txt=out.decode(errors='replace')
    # find flame rows
    import re
    for row in [4,5,6,7]:
        m=re.search(rf'\x1b\[{row};1H(.*?)(?=\x1b\[\d+;1H)', txt, re.DOTALL)
        if m:
            seg=m.group(1)
            # extract blocks
            blocks=re.findall(r'\x1b\[38;2;.*?m([^\x1b]*?)(?=\x1b)', seg)
            print(f" row{row} blocks: {[repr(b) for b in blocks]}")
    print("---")
    os.unlink(fname)

cap_raw(b"a;b 10 20\n")
cap_raw(b"foo 10 extra\n")

# flamelens

flamelens is an interactive flamegraph viewer for the terminal.

Description

flamelens reads folded stacks (stack traces aggregated in the "folded" format) and
renders an interactive flamegraph in a terminal UI so you can explore profiling data
without opening a browser.

Usage

Run flamelens with a folded stacks filename, or pipe folded stacks data to it:

flamelens <folded-stacks-filename>

or

cat folded-stacks.txt | flamelens

Live mode

flamelens can attach to a running process to display a live flamegraph (when supported):

flamelens --pid <pid-of-process>

Viewing perf data

You can generate folded stacks from perf and pipe them to flamelens, for example:

perf script -i perf.data | <tool-to-collapse-perf-output> | flamelens

Key bindings

- h/j/k/l or arrow keys: Navigate cursor for frame selection
- f: Scroll down
- b: Scroll up
- G: Scroll to bottom
- g: Scroll to top
- Enter: Zoom in on the selected frame
- Esc: Reset zoom
- /<regex>: Find and highlight frames matching the regex
- #: Find and highlight frames matching the selected frame
- n: Jump to next match
- N: Jump to previous match
- r: Reset to default view
- z (in Live mode): Freeze the flamegraph
- q (or Ctrl + c): Exit

Examples

- Open a folded stacks file:

  flamelens folded.txt

- Pipe collapsed perf output:

  perf script -i perf.data | inferno-collapse-perf | flamelens

Notes

This README intentionally omits build- and implementation-specific details.

use crossterm::event::{self, Event, KeyCode, KeyModifiers};
use ratatui::{prelude::*, widgets::*};
use std::io::{self, Read};
use std::time::{Instant, Duration};
use std::collections::HashMap;

#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
struct Node {
    name: String,
    total: u64,
    children: Vec<Node>,
}

impl Node {
    fn new(name: String) -> Self {
        Node { name, total: 0, children: Vec::new() }
    }
    fn find_child_mut(&mut self, name: &str) -> Option<&mut Node> {
        self.children.iter_mut().find(|c| c.name == name)
    }
    fn sort_recursive(&mut self) {
        self.children.sort_by(|a,b| b.total.cmp(&a.total));
        for c in &mut self.children { c.sort_recursive(); }
    }
}

fn parse_folded(content: &str) -> (Node, u64) {
    let mut root = Node::new("all".to_string());
    let mut total: u64 = 0;
    for line in content.split('\n') {
        if line.is_empty() {
            // empty line from trailing \n? Actually split gives last empty after final \n, ignore
            // But lines with only ""? They have no space, will be ignored below
        }
        // find last space (0x20)
        if let Some(idx) = line.rfind(' ') {
            let stack_raw = &line[..idx];
            let count_str = &line[idx+1..];
            if count_str.is_empty() { continue; }
            if !count_str.bytes().all(|b| b.is_ascii_digit()) { continue; }
            let count: u64 = match count_str.parse() {
                Ok(v) => v,
                Err(_) => continue,
            };
            // stack must be non-empty after trimming trailing spaces? Actually stack_raw may have trailing spaces from double-space case
            // Trim trailing spaces (0x20) only? Preserve leading
            let mut stack = stack_raw;
            // trim trailing spaces
            while stack.ends_with(' ') {
                stack = &stack[..stack.len()-1];
            }
            if stack.is_empty() { continue; }
            // split by ';' preserving empties
            let frames: Vec<&str> = stack.split(';').collect();
            // add to tree
            total = total.saturating_add(count);
            root.total = root.total.saturating_add(count);
            let mut cur = &mut root;
            for f in frames {
                // f may contain spaces inside, preserve as is (including leading/trailing? For double-space case, trailing already trimmed at stack level, so frames have no trailing extra)
                // But what about frames with trailing spaces inside? e.g., "a;b ;c" -> frame "b " with trailing? Preserve? Our stack trim only trims end of whole stack, not each frame. So "b " preserved. Good.
                let fname = f.to_string();
                // find or create
                let child = if let Some(pos) = cur.children.iter().position(|c| c.name == fname) {
                    &mut cur.children[pos]
                } else {
                    cur.children.push(Node::new(fname.clone()));
                    cur.children.last_mut().unwrap()
                };
                child.total = child.total.saturating_add(count);
                cur = child;
            }
        } else {
            continue;
        }
    }
    (root, total)
}

use clap::{Arg, Command};
use crossterm::event::{self, Event, KeyCode, KeyModifiers};
use ratatui::{prelude::*, widgets::*};
use std::io::{self, Read};
use std::time::{Instant, Duration};
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
struct Node { name: String, total: u64, children: Vec<Node> }
impl Node {
    fn new(name: String) -> Self { Node { name, total: 0, children: Vec::new() } }
    fn sort_recursive(&mut self) {
        self.children.sort_by(|a,b| b.total.cmp(&a.total));
        for c in &mut self.children { c.sort_recursive(); }
    }
}
fn parse_folded(content: &str) -> (Node, u64) {
    let mut root = Node::new("all".to_string());
    let mut total: u64 = 0;
    for line in content.split('\n') {
        if let Some(idx) = line.rfind(' ') {
            let stack_raw = &line[..idx];
            let count_str = &line[idx+1..];
            if count_str.is_empty() { continue; }
            if !count_str.bytes().all(|b| b.is_ascii_digit()) { continue; }
            let count: u64 = match count_str.parse() { Ok(v) => v, Err(_) => continue };
            let mut stack = stack_raw;
            while stack.ends_with(' ') { stack = &stack[..stack.len()-1]; }
            if stack.is_empty() { continue; }
            let frames: Vec<&str> = stack.split(';').collect();
            total = total.saturating_add(count);
            root.total = root.total.saturating_add(count);
            let mut cur = &mut root;
            for f in frames {
                let fname = f.to_string();
                let pos = cur.children.iter().position(|c| c.name == fname);
                let child = if let Some(p) = pos { &mut cur.children[p] } else { cur.children.push(Node::new(fname)); cur.children.last_mut().unwrap() };
                child.total = child.total.saturating_add(count);
                cur = child;
            }
        }
    }
    (root, total)
}
// color helpers
fn hash_str(s: &str) -> u64 {
    use std::collections::hash_map::DefaultHasher;
    use std::hash::{Hash, Hasher};
    let mut h = DefaultHasher::new();
    s.hash(&mut h);
    h.finish()
}
fn bg_for(name: &str, depth: usize) -> (u8,u8,u8) {
    if name == "all" && depth==0 {
        // will be overridden for selected? Actually unselected all is 205,3,0
        // For selected, white. For unselected, return 205,3,0
        return (205,3,0);
    }
    // combine name + depth for hash to get depth-dependent colors
    let combined = format!("{}:{}", name, depth);
    let h = hash_str(&combined);
    // map to warm palette: use h to pick r,g,b in warm range
    // Observed warm: R 200-255, G 10-250, B 2-55
    // Use h bits
    let r = 200 + ((h >> 16) % 56) as u8; // 200-255
    let g = ((h >> 8) % 240) as u8; // 0-239, but need warm? For warm, g varies widely
    let b = ((h) % 50 + 2) as u8; // 2-51
    // tweak to match observed? For now use this
    // Actually to get closer, use h % 3 for base?
    (r,g,b)
}
fn fg_for_bg(r:u8,g:u8,b:u8) -> (u8,u8,u8) {
    let lum = 0.299*(r as f32)+0.587*(g as f32)+0.114*(b as f32);
    if lum > 150.0 { (10,10,10) } else { (225,225,225) }
}

use std::io::{self, Read};

struct Node { name: String, total: u64, children: Vec<Node> }

        self.children.sort_by(|a,b| b.total.cmp(&a.total));

    let mut root = Node::new("all".to_string());
    let mut total: u64 = 0;
    for line in content.split('\n') {
        if let Some(idx) = line.rfind(' ') {

            let count_str = &line[idx+1..];
            if count_str.is_empty() { continue; }
            if !count_str.bytes().all(|b| b.is_ascii_digit()) { continue; }
            let count: u64 = match count_str.parse() { Ok(v) => v, Err(_) => continue };
            let mut stack = stack_raw;
            while stack.ends_with(' ') { stack = &stack[..stack.len()-1]; }
            if stack.is_empty() { continue; }
            let frames: Vec<&str> = stack.split(';').collect();
            total = total.saturating_add(count);
            root.total = root.total.saturating_add(count);
            let mut cur = &mut root;
            for f in frames {
                let fname = f.to_string();
                let pos = cur.children.iter().position(|c| c.name == fname);
                let child = if let Some(p) = pos { &mut cur.children[p] } else { cur.children.push(Node::new(fname)); cur.children.last_mut().unwrap() };
                child.total = child.total.saturating_add(count);
                cur = child;
            }
        }
    }
    (root, total)
}
fn main() -> io::Result<()> {
    let matches = Command::new("flamelens").version("0.3.1")
        .arg(Arg::new("sorted").long("sorted").action(clap::ArgAction::SetTrue).help("Whether to sort the stacks by time spent"))
        .arg(Arg::new("echo").long("echo").action(clap::ArgAction::SetTrue).help("Print data to stdout on exit. Useful when piping to other tools"))
        .arg(Arg::new("debug").long("debug").action(clap::ArgAction::SetTrue).help("Show debug info"))
        .arg(Arg::new("FILENAME").value_name("FILENAME").help("Profile data filename"))
        .get_matches();
    let sorted = matches.get_flag("sorted");
    let echo = matches.get_flag("echo");
    let debug = matches.get_flag("debug");
    let filename_opt: Option<String> = matches.get_one::<String>("FILENAME").cloned();
    let (raw_data, display_name) = if let Some(fname) = filename_opt.clone() {

    } else {
        let mut buf = String::new();
        let _ = io::stdin().read_to_string(&mut buf);
        (buf, "stdin".to_string())
    };
    let (mut root, total) = parse_folded(&raw_data);
    if sorted { root.sort_recursive(); }
    let mut terminal = ratatui::try_init()?;
    let res = run_app(&mut terminal, root, total, sorted, echo, debug, display_name);
    ratatui::restore();
    if echo { print!("{}\n", raw_data); }
    res
}
fn run_app(terminal: &mut ratatui::DefaultTerminal, root: Node, total: u64, _sorted: bool, _echo: bool, debug: bool, display_name: String) -> io::Result<()> {
    Ok(())
}

                out+=d

                        d=os.read(master, 16384)
                        if not d: break
                        out+=d
                    except: break
                break
    drain(0.8)

        except: pass

            while time.time()<end:
                r,_,_ = select.select([master], [], [], 0.2)
                if not r: break
                try:
                    d=os.read(master, 16384)
                    if not d: break
                    out+=d
                except: break
        except: pass
    try: os.close(master)
    except: pass
    try: p.wait(timeout=1)
    except: pass
    return out, p.returncode

def grid(raw, rows=24, cols=80):
    txt=raw.decode(errors='replace')
    g=[[' ']*cols for _ in range(rows)]
    cur_r,cur_c=0,0
    i=0
    n=len(txt)
    while i<n:
        if txt[i]=='\x1b' and i+1<n and txt[i+1]=='[':
            j=i+2
            while j<n and (txt[j].isdigit() or txt[j] in ';?:'):
                j+=1
            if j>=n: break
            cmd=txt[j]
            params=txt[i+2:j]
            if cmd=='H':
                if ';' in params:
                    r,c=params.split(';')
                    cur_r=int(r)-1;cur_c=int(c)-1
                elif params=='': cur_r,cur_c=0,0
            elif cmd=='J':
                if params=='2':
                    g=[[' ']*cols for _ in range(rows)];cur_r,cur_c=0,0
            i=j+1
        elif txt[i]=='\x1b' and i+1<n and txt[i+1]=='(':
            i+=3
        else:

            if ch=='\n': cur_r+=1;cur_c=0
            elif ch=='\r': cur_c=0
            else:
                if 0<=cur_r<rows and 0<=cur_c<cols:
                    g[cur_r][cur_c]=ch;cur_c+=1
                    if cur_c>=cols: cur_c=0;cur_r+=1
            i+=1
    return [' '.join([]) or ''.join(r) for r in g]

content=b"main;foo;bar 10\nmain;foo;baz 20\nmain;qux 5\n"

def run_bin(bin_path, args, bulk=b""):
    master, slave = pty.openpty()
    winsz = struct.pack("HHHH", 24, 80, 0, 0)
    fcntl.ioctl(slave, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, winsz)
    p = subprocess.Popen([bin_path]+args, stdin=slave, stdout=slave, stderr=slave)
    os.close(slave)
    flags = fcntl.fcntl(master, fcntl.F_GETFL)
    fcntl.fcntl(master, fcntl.F_SETFL, flags | os.O_NONBLOCK)
    out=b""
    def drain(dur):
        nonlocal out
        end=time.time()+dur
        while time.time()<end:
            r,_,_ = select.select([master], [], [], max(0, end-time.time()))
            if not r: break
            try:
                d=os.read(master, 16384)
                if not d: break
                out+=d
            except: break
    drain(0.8)
    if bulk:
        os.write(master, bulk)
        drain(0.8)
    if p.poll() is None:

        time.sleep(0.3)
        if p.poll() is None: p.kill()
    os.close(master)
    p.wait(timeout=1)
    return out

            cmd=txt[j]

    master, slave = pty.openpty()

    fcntl.ioctl(slave, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, winsz)

    except: pass
    os.unlink(fname)

//! Terminal initialization and restoration functions.
//!
//! This module provides a set of convenience functions for initializing and restoring terminal
//! state when creating Ratatui applications. These functions handle the common setup and teardown
//! tasks required for terminal user interfaces.
//!
//! All functions in this module use the [`CrosstermBackend`] by default, which provides excellent
//! cross-platform compatibility and is the recommended backend for most applications. The
//! [`DefaultTerminal`] type alias encapsulates this choice, providing a ready-to-use terminal
//! configuration that works well across different operating systems. For more information about
//! backend choices and alternatives, see the [`backend`](`crate::backend`) module.
//!
//! Once you have initialized a terminal using the functions in this module, you can use it to
//! [draw the UI](`crate#drawing-the-ui`) and [handle events](`crate#handling-events`). For more
//! information about building widgets for your application, see the [`widgets`](`crate::widgets`)
//! module.
//!
//! **Note**: All functions and types in this module are re-exported at the crate root for
//! convenience, so you can call `ratatui::run()`, `ratatui::init()`, etc. instead of
//! `ratatui::init::run()`, `ratatui::init::init()`, etc.
//!
//! # Which function should I start with?
//!
//! Start with the simplest path that fits your application:
//!
//! 1. Use [`run`] for the normal case: Ratatui owns setup and cleanup around your application
//!    closure.
//! 2. Move to [`init`] / [`restore`] when you want explicit control over setup, teardown, or event
//!    loop structure.
//! 3. Use [`try_init`] / [`try_restore`] when you want the same control but need explicit error
//!    handling instead of panicking or printing cleanup failures.
//! 4. Use [`init_with_options`] / [`try_init_with_options`] when you need a custom
//!    [`TerminalOptions`] such as inline or fixed viewports.
//! 5. Construct [`Terminal`] manually only when these helpers do not match the backend or terminal
//!    lifecycle you need.
//!
//! # Available Types and Functions
//!
//! ## Types
//!
//! - [`DefaultTerminal`] - A type alias for `Terminal<CrosstermBackend<Stdout>>`, providing a
//!   reasonable default terminal configuration for most applications. All initialization functions
//!   return this type.
//!
//! ## Functions
//!
//! The module provides several related functions that handle different initialization scenarios:
//!
//! - [`run`] - Initializes a terminal, runs a closure, and automatically restores the terminal
//!   state. This is the simplest way to run a Ratatui application and handles all setup and cleanup
//!   automatically.
//! - [`init`] - Creates a terminal with reasonable defaults including alternate screen and raw
//!   mode. Panics on failure.
//! - [`try_init`] - Same as [`init`] but returns a `Result` instead of panicking.
//! - [`init_with_options`] - Creates a terminal with custom [`TerminalOptions`], enabling raw mode
//!   but not alternate screen. Panics on failure.
//! - [`try_init_with_options`] - Same as [`init_with_options`] but returns a `Result` instead of
//!   panicking.
//! - [`restore`] - Restores the terminal to its original state. Prints errors to stderr but does
//!   not panic.
//! - [`try_restore`] - Same as [`restore`] but returns a `Result` instead of printing errors.
//!
//! # Usage Guide
//!
//! Start with the normal fullscreen application path:
//!
//! ```rust,no_run
//! fn main() -> std::io::Result<()> {
//!     ratatui::run(|terminal| {
//!         loop {
//!             terminal.draw(|frame| frame.render_widget("Hello, world!", frame.area()))?;
//!             if crossterm::event::read()?.is_key_press() {
//!                 break Ok(());
//!             }
//!         }
//!     })
//! }
//! ```
//!
//! Then add resize-aware redraws to the event loop:
//!
//! ```rust,no_run
//! use crossterm::event::{self, Event, KeyCode, KeyEventKind};
//!
//! fn main() -> std::io::Result<()> {
//!     ratatui::run(|terminal| {
//!         loop {
//!             terminal.draw(|frame| {
//!                 frame.render_widget("Resize the terminal or press q to quit", frame.area());
//!             })?;
//!
//!             match event::read()? {
//!                 Event::Resize(_, _) => {
//!                     // The next `draw` pass re-renders the UI at the new size.
//!                 }
//!                 Event::Key(key)
//!                     if key.kind == KeyEventKind::Press && key.code == KeyCode::Char('q') =>
//!                 {
//!                     break Ok(());
//!                 }
//!                 _ => {}
//!             }
//!         }
//!     })
//! }
//! ```
//!
//! Reach for [`init`] / [`restore`] when you want manual control over setup and teardown:
//!
//! ```rust,no_run
//! // Using init() - panics on failure
//! let mut terminal = ratatui::init();
//! // ... app logic ...
//! ratatui::restore();
//!
//! // Using try_init() - returns Result for custom error handling
//! let mut terminal = ratatui::try_init()?;
//! // ... app logic ...
//! ratatui::try_restore()?;
//! # Ok::<(), std::io::Error>(())
//! ```
//!
//! Use [`init_with_options`] when the UI should not use the normal fullscreen path, for example
//! for an inline UI that continues to share the terminal with earlier output:
//!
//! ```rust,no_run
//! use crossterm::event::{self, Event, KeyCode, KeyEventKind};
//! use ratatui::widgets::Widget;
//! use ratatui::{TerminalOptions, Viewport};
//!
//! let options = TerminalOptions {
//!     viewport: Viewport::Inline(10),
//! };
//!
//! let mut terminal = ratatui::init_with_options(options);
//!
//! terminal.insert_before(1, |buf| {
//!     "> Ready".render(buf.area, buf);
//! })?;
//!
//! loop {
//!     terminal.draw(|frame| {
//!         frame.render_widget("Inline UI lives below earlier terminal output", frame.area());
//!     })?;
//!
//!     if matches!(
//!         event::read()?,
//!         Event::Key(key)
//!             if key.kind == KeyEventKind::Press && key.code == KeyCode::Char('q')
//!     ) {
//!         break;
//!     }
//! }
//!
//! ratatui::restore();
//!
//! // Using try_init_with_options() - returns Result for custom error handling
//! let options = TerminalOptions {
//!     viewport: Viewport::Inline(10),
//! };
//! let mut terminal = ratatui::try_init_with_options(options)?;
//! terminal.draw(|frame| {
//!     frame.render_widget("Inline UI", frame.area());
//! })?;
//! ratatui::try_restore()?;

/// Try to initialize a terminal using reasonable defaults for most applications.
///
/// This function will attempt to create a [`DefaultTerminal`] and initialize it with the following

/// - Alternate screen buffer enabled
/// - A panic hook is installed that restores the terminal before panicking.

///
/// Ensure that this method is called *after* your app installs any other panic hooks to ensure the
/// terminal is restored before the other hooks are called.

/// function will ensure that any failures during initialization will restore the terminal before
/// panicking. This function is provided for cases where you need to handle the error yourself.

    set_panic_hook();
    enable_raw_mode()?;
    execute!(stdout(), EnterAlternateScreen)?;
    let backend = CrosstermBackend::new(stdout());
    Terminal::new(backend)
